options: Glob with a pattern like **/*.spec.ts, since the requirement is matching file paths by naming convention across the whole repository
Grep for the string "describe(" across the repository, since every genuine Playwright spec file will contain at least one test suite declaration
Read each package's test directory in sequence, building the inventory from the directory listings that come back from every package
Write a manifest file first and have the agent update it whenever it happens to encounter spec files during its other exploration tasks
optionExplanations: Correct. This is a file path pattern-matching task, which is exactly what Glob is for: **/*.spec.ts returns every file matching the naming convention across the monorepo in one call, giving a complete inventory keyed by location — precisely what a per-package coverage report needs.

Grep searches file contents, and "describe(" appears in unit tests, integration tests, and shared helpers too — the inventory would be polluted with non-Playwright files while any spec file with a different structure is missed. The requirement is defined by file naming, so the path-matching tool fits.

Sequential directory reads re-implement Glob slowly and fragilely: packages nest their test folders differently, some co-locate specs beside source, and each read spends context on listings a single pattern match replaces. It also breaks silently when a package deviates from the assumed layout.

An opportunistically updated manifest is never complete — coverage gaps are exactly the packages the agent has no other reason to visit — and it converts a one-call query into a stale artifact requiring ongoing maintenance. Discovery should be exhaustive and on demand.
principle: Glob matches file paths by pattern; Grep searches contents
relatedConcept: Finding files by naming convention (e.g., **/*.spec.ts) is Glob's job; content-based search belongs to Grep.
overallExplanation: Inventorying files by naming convention is file path pattern matching — Glob with **/*.spec.ts. Grep would search contents and both over- and under-match, while manual directory walks and opportunistic manifests are slower, fragile substitutes for a single pattern query.

objective: Select and apply built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) effectively
question: Your agent must confirm a deprecated formatCurrency function is safe to delete. A Grep for formatCurrency finds only two callers — but the codebase wraps utilities in modules that re-export them under new names like formatMoney and toDisplayPrice, so most usage is hidden behind aliases. What search strategy gives a trustworthy answer?
options: First identify every name the wrapper modules export for the function, then Grep for each exported name across the codebase to find all indirect callers
Trust the original Grep result, since two callers means the function is effectively unused and the wrapper modules will fail fast if anything breaks
Glob for files named *wrapper* or *utils* and read them, since the alias definitions will be concentrated in files following those naming conventions
Delete the function on a branch and let the compiler surface every break, since type errors are a more reliable usage census than any text search
optionExplanations: Correct. Tracing usage across wrapper modules is a two-step search: first enumerate all the exported names and aliases the wrappers publish for the function, then search for each of those names across the codebase. Only the union of those searches counts the indirect callers that a single-name Grep structurally misses.

The two-caller count is exactly the artifact of the aliasing problem: every formatMoney and toDisplayPrice call site is invisible to a search for the original name. Concluding safety from a search known to be blind to the dominant usage pattern is how deprecated-code deletions break production.

Filename conventions are a guess about where aliases live, not a census of what they are called: wrappers may sit in index files or feature modules with arbitrary names. Even when the files are found, the essential step is still extracting the exported names and searching for each — which this option never reaches.

Compile-and-see only works when everything flows through static, typed imports — dynamic access, string-keyed lookups, and untyped boundaries all pass the compiler silently. It also inverts the workflow: a deletion experiment as the discovery mechanism, with the census arriving as a pile of errors.
principle: trace aliased usage: enumerate exported names first, then search each
relatedConcept: Wrapper modules hide callers behind re-exported names; a trustworthy census greps for every alias, not just the original.
overallExplanation: When wrapper modules re-export a function under new names, first identify all exported names, then Grep for each across the codebase — the union finds the indirect callers. A single-name search, filename guessing, or compiler roulette all undercount real usage.

objective: Select and apply built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) effectively
question: Your agent must remove the deprecated feature flag ENABLE_LEGACY_CHECKOUT from a large repository: every reference must be found, and each conditional that reads the flag must be carefully unwound in place without disturbing surrounding code. Which two built-in tool applications fit this task? (Choose two.)
options: Use Grep to search file contents for ENABLE_LEGACY_CHECKOUT so every referencing file is found regardless of its location or name
Use Edit with unique anchor text in each affected file to make the targeted modifications while leaving the rest of each file untouched
Use Glob with the pattern **/ENABLE_LEGACY_CHECKOUT* to locate the files whose contents reference the deprecated feature flag
Use Write to regenerate each affected file in full from the model's memory of its contents, avoiding any dependency on anchor text matching
optionExplanations: Correct. Finding every reference to a known string across a repository is content search — Grep's exact purpose. It returns all files containing the flag no matter what they are named or where they live, which is the completeness the removal requires.

Correct. Unwinding each conditional is a targeted, surgical change in an otherwise untouched file — Edit's exact purpose, using unique anchor text to locate each modification precisely. Whole-file rewrites are unnecessary risk when the changes are localized.

Glob matches file path patterns, not file contents — a flag referenced inside checkout.ts produces no path containing the flag's name, so this pattern would find nothing useful. Content search is Grep's job; using Glob here confuses the two tools' domains.

Regenerating whole files from memory risks silently dropping or altering code far from the flag, precisely what "without disturbing surrounding code" forbids. Read + Write is a fallback for when Edit lacks unique anchors, and even then it starts from Read, never from recall.
principle: Grep finds content; Edit modifies it surgically in place
relatedConcept: Repo-wide reference removal pairs content search (Grep) with targeted anchored modification (Edit), not path matching or file regeneration.
overallExplanation: Removing a flag repo-wide pairs Grep — content search that finds every referencing file — with Edit — anchored, targeted in-place changes. Glob matches paths rather than contents, and regenerating files from memory risks collateral changes the task explicitly forbids.

objective: Select and apply built-in tools (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob) effectively
question: Reviewing agent traces, you find that when asked to change a single default value in a 900-line configuration module, the agent regenerated the entire file with Write — and silently dropped two unrelated sections in the process. The target line contains a distinctive, unique setting name. How should the agent have handled the change?
options: Use Edit anchored on the unique setting text for a targeted modification, reserving Read followed by Write for cases where no unique anchor exists
Use Write as it did, but only after instructing the model to reproduce every other line exactly so no unrelated content can be lost in regeneration
Use Bash to append a corrected copy of the setting at the end of the file, overriding the earlier default without touching the original line
Split the module into several smaller files first so future whole-file regenerations carry less risk of dropping unrelated sections
optionExplanations: Correct. Edit is the tool for targeted modifications using unique text matching — with a distinctive anchor available, it changes exactly the intended line and structurally cannot touch the rest of the file. Read + Write exists as the fallback for when unique anchors are unavailable, which is not the case here.

An instruction to reproduce 900 lines faithfully is a probabilistic hope layered on the exact failure just observed — regeneration omissions are silent, and no prompt wording makes full-file recall reliable. The tool selection is the defect; Edit removes the reproduction step entirely.

Appending a duplicate setting leaves two definitions in the file whose precedence depends on parser behavior — later-wins, first-wins, or a duplicate-key error. It converts a clean one-line change into a latent ambiguity that will confuse both tooling and future readers.

Restructuring the module to make a risky technique less damaging accepts the wrong premise: whole-file regeneration was never the right operation for a one-line change. The safe tool already exists; reorganizing the codebase to accommodate the unsafe one is backwards.
principle: prefer Edit for targeted changes; Read + Write is the no-unique-anchor fallback
relatedConcept: Edit's unique text matching makes small modifications safe; whole-file Write regeneration risks silent content loss.
overallExplanation: Single-line changes with a unique anchor belong to Edit, which structurally cannot disturb the rest of the file. Whole-file Write regeneration risks silent omissions, and Read + Write is the fallback only when Edit's unique-anchor requirement cannot be met.
